tweets.text:
7/3 – Temecula, CA
What began as a routine traffic stop quickly escalated when Border Patrol agents spotted suspicious indicators that warranted further investigation. A K9 alert led to a search of the vehicle, revealing 5 bricks of cocaine—7 kilograms in total—concealed in the trunk. Estimated street value: $119,000.

The driver was taken into custody and now faces federal prosecution under 21 U.S.C. § 841 for possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance.

Every stop counts. Every seizure matters.

tweets.text:
MEXICAN VISA HOLDER CAUGHT WITH OVER $700K IN COCAINE!

SAN CLEMENTE, CA – On 7/9, USBP agents stopped a sedan near I-5 during a routine highway patrol. Inside the trunk? A duffel bag packed with 37 bundles of cocaine—nearly 100 pounds of this deadly drug. Agents seized the narcotics and turned the case over to DEA. The driver’s B1/B2 visa was immediately revoked, and he now faces removal proceedings.

A visa is a privilege—not a right. Break the law, and you lose that privilege.

VIOLENT MS-13 GANG MEMBER ARRESTED IN MICHIGAN!

On Sunday, USBP agents and Sterling Heights PD removed a dangerous Salvadoran national from our streets. Officers responded to a hotel fight and called Border Patrol for backup. During questioning, the suspect admitted to being an MS-13 gang member and revealed he had served 20 years in El Salvador for murder. He also has a prior drug possession arrest.  

He’s now in custody and awaiting removal proceedings.
Removing violent criminals isn’t optional—it’s essential to keeping America safe.
